what: is Sol's exact stage bound by staging routed key blocks into shared memory or by computing them: three compile-time probe variants of sol_exact_kernel timed against the kernel as written, on captured q/k/v, all heads, the plain arm of bench/profile_sol_stages.py
model: MiniMax H3, int8 convrot checkpoint, base 16-step t2v captures
conditions: 2026-09-17, RTX 4090, card alone, comfy-kitchen fork h3-build b532e28 plus the probe commit on local branch probe/exact-stage-vs-compute (not pushed, never installed; unpacked wheels loaded by PYTHONPATH). GPU performance counters are admin-only on this machine, so ncu could not be used; this is the counter-free substitute.
reading: Staging alone costs about 0.70 of the full exact stage and compute alone about 0.91, with a floor of about 0.03 when both are removed. They overlap: the one-block-ahead async staging hides most of the copy time behind compute. Compute is the critical path. Removing staging ENTIRELY would save about a tenth, which bounds what sharing staged blocks between neighbouring query blocks (Comfy-Org/comfy-kitchen#184, measured there on HIP) can give on this card. Making compute free would save at most three tenths, because staging then becomes the critical path. So no single kernel change to this stage is worth more than roughly a tenth to a fifth of it; the larger levers are outside the kernel (start_percent, routed density).
caveats: Variants 1-3 produce wrong outputs by construction. Variant 2 computes on stale tiles, which costs the same arithmetic; variant 1's copies have no reader but are still issued (its time is far above the floor). Two cells, one step.
